# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-34 (Extended v223)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to summer Year 9. Key Paris locations: Rue Plumet, Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue de l'Homme Armé No. 6, Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Champs-Élysées, Rue Saint-Honoré, Luxembourg Garden, Quai aux Fleurs, Rue du Temple, sewers (Sainte-Avoye, Louvre, Montmartre, belt, Amelot, Beautreillis), Marais, Blancs-Manteaux, Rue Culture-Sainte-Catherine, Rue de l'Écharpe, Rue Pavée, Rue des Trois-Pavillons, Saint-Paul church, Rue Beautreillis near Arsenal, Grand Sewer, Rue de l'Hôpital, Père-Lachaise cemetery. English locations: Kelmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Dungate, Ravenmere, Staveford, Wilwick, Salcombe, Wilholt, Torton, Yarlby, Gagny, Lagny, Gulhaven.

## English Subplot Summary

**Established facts through summer Year 9**: Semor swore to Isric Thornmere to rebuild fallen wall at Kelmere (summer Year 9). Solemn promises: Elra gave Matho promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven; Pelia gave Fenelle promise to plant orchard above Salcombe (summer Year 7); Movie swore to Nerine to plant orchard above Wilholt (autumn Year 7); Yera Haskick swore to Nerine Prydenridge to repair chapel roof at Kelmere (winter Year 8); Kassa Stenson kept promise to Taric Corrley: wall at Yarlby rebuilt by harvest; Kassa's husband swore to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe.

**Chapter 33-34 domestic observations**: Pelde Stenson, Dalis Stenworth, Davus, Rimor Corrford, Kassa Brackick, Volan Stenworth tired or aching. Multiple residents sorted old letters, hummed tunes while scrubbing steps, read almanacs mispronouncing saints. Istho Stenworth counted coins twice (came up penny short). Children chased hoops. Bees hummed in lavender. Frost silvered hedges. Gulls quarreled over fish heads. Rain threatened but held off. Carts creaked with turnips. Wind came off water with salt and tar smell. Baker's boy late multiple times.

**Migrations and marriages**: Luena Stenenridge's only son packed single trunk, moved from Ostcombe to Elmhaven. Pelde Stenworth married Sebin Brackick at Torton before autumn was out; couple lived in Torton thereafter. Fewyn Stenworth packed single trunk and moved from Gulhaven to Yarlby. Havus went to live in Yarlby.

**Stenenridge mill ledger**: Late one night Kassa Brackick confided to Davus that Stenenridge mill ledger was rewritten after flood.

**Chapter 34 detailed activities**: Elra Corrford complained of aching back, watched clouds (predicted rain wrongly), hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step, counted coins twice (came up penny short), read almanac aloud mispronouncing saints, mended torn sleeve by window, said little. Someone chalked crooked sun on forge wall. Tatho Brackick (Wilholt harbor town) watched clouds (predicted rain wrongly), counted coins twice (came up penny short), mended torn sleeve by window, said little, argued with carter over price of sack of oats, told Yewyn Haskick that fire at Dunstead granary was set on purpose. Yewyn Haskick laughed at story nobody else found funny, counted coins twice (came up penny short), read almanac aloud mispronouncing saints, was told by Rinelle Corrley "You look tired" (did not deny). Volia Brackick's youngest son talked weeks of going to Staveford but stayed where he was. Kadrek Brackick hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step. Rimor Corrford read almanac aloud mispronouncing saints, complained price of salt was scandal (Vesmira Thornmere agreed). Baker's boy late again; line at oven grew long.

## Marseilles/Pharaon Ship Subplot (Excerpts 1770-1783)

**Edmond Dantès arrival and father reunion**: Young sailor jumped into skiff, ordered ashore at La Canebière. Shipowner Danglars watched him disappear into throng on famous street. Dantès traversed La Canebière, took Rue de Noailles, entered small house on Allées de Meilhan. Ascended four flights of dark staircase, found father in room training nasturtiums and clematis at window. Father did not know _Pharaon_ had arrived. Dantès embraced him: "Father—dear father!"

**Dantès announces promotion**: Told father Captain Leclere is dead; probable he shall have his place with M. Morrel's aid. Captain at twenty, hundred louis pay, share in profits. God forgive him for rejoicing at happiness derived from misery of others; could not pretend to lament it.

**Money and Caderousse**: Emptied pockets—dozen gold pieces, five or six five-franc pieces, smaller coin. Negligently said money not his; was expressing fears he wanted many things in absence. Told Caderousse money at his service if needed. Directed father to put money in box. Remarked greedy glance in Caderousse's dark eyes.

**Fernand and Mercédès tragic romance**: Fernand begged Mercédès to repeat refusal, saying he dreamed ten years of marriage and losing hope ruined existence. Mercédès replied she never encouraged hope; always said she loved him as brother; heart belonged to another. Cannot reproach her with slightest coquetry.

**Conscription and Mercédès' circumstances**: Fernand included in conscription, at liberty only on sufferance. Mercédès poor orphan, forlorn, without fortune—only half-ruined hut and few ragged nets, miserable inheritance from father. Mother dead a year; subsisted almost entirely on public charity. Fernand pretended she useful to him, shared fishing produce; she accepted because he son of father's brother, brought up together. Fish she sold, flax she spun—felt keenly this was charity.

**Fernand's final plea and Mercédès' threat**: Fernand asked once for all if this her final determination. **Mercédès declared: if misfortune occur to Edmond, she would ascend highest point of Cape de Morgiou and cast herself headlong from it.** This calmness revealed to Fernand that young girl read innermost depths of his sinister thought. Fernand, as if fascinated, came slowly towards Edmond, offered hand. His hatred, powerless though furious wave, broken against strong ascendancy Mercédès exercised over him. Scarcely had he touched Edmond's hand when he felt he done all he could do, rushed hastily out of house.

**Edmond and Mercédès reunion**: Fernand pale and trembling, drew back like traveller at sight of serpent, fell into chair. Edmond and Mercédès clasped in each other's arms. Burning Marseilles sun covered them with flood of light. Intense happiness isolated them from rest of world; spoke in broken words expressing joy so extreme seemed sorrow. Suddenly Edmond saw gloomy, pale, threatening countenance of Fernand defined in shadow. Young Catalan placed hand on knife at belt. Dantès extended other hand to Catalan with cordial air. Fernand remained mute and trembling. Edmond cast eyes scrutinizingly at agitated Mercédès, then gloomy Fernand. This look told him all; his anger waxed hot.

**Caderousse and Danglars at tavern**: Caderousse called to Fernand rushing like madman, afraid he would throw himself into sea. Said when man has friends, not only to offer glass of wine but prevent swallowing three or four pints water unnecessarily. At river crossing at Dungate, Caderousse winked at Danglars: "Fernand, whom you see here, is good and brave Catalan, one of best fishermen in Marseilles, in love with very fine girl, named Mercédès; but it appears fine girl in love with mate of _Pharaon_; and as _Pharaon_ arrived today—why, you understand!" Caderousse claimed saw two lovers by wall in direction of Catalans, embracing, holding hands.

**Fernand's violent impulse constrained**: Fernand, probably excited beyond bearing, pricked by Danglars as bull by bandilleros, about to rush out, risen from seat, collecting himself to dash headlong upon rival. Mercédès, smiling and graceful, lifted lovely head, looked at them with clear and bright eyes. At this Fernand recollected her threat of dying if Edmond died, dropped heavily on seat. Danglars looked at two men—one brutalized by liquor, other overwhelmed with love.

**Danglars' sinister plan**: Danglars muttered: "I shall get nothing from these fools; I am very much afraid of being here between drunkard and coward. Here's envious fellow making himself boozy on wine when ought nursing wrath, and here is fool who sees woman he loves stolen from under his nose and takes on like big baby. Yet this Catalan has eyes that glisten like those of vengeful Spaniards, Sicilians, and Calabrians, and other has fists big enough crush ox at one blow. Unquestionably, Edmond's star in ascendant, and he will marry splendid girl—he will be captain, too, and laugh at us all, unless"—sinister smile passed over Danglars' lips—"unless I take hand in affair."

**Danglars' scheme with letter**: Said to someone (presumably Caderousse): "To Paris, no doubt to deliver letter which grand marshal gave him. Ah, this letter gives me idea—capital idea! Ah; Dantès, my friend, you are not yet registered number one on board good ship _Pharaon_;" then turning towards Edmond walking away, "A pleasant journey," he cried.

## Marius and Cosette: Courtship to Death Vigil

**Spring Year 6 confessions**: Marius revealed orphan status, lawyer profession, father colonel-hero. Cosette revealed convent upbringing, dead mother, father M. Fauchelevent.

**Barricade and rescue (June Year 6)**: Éponine died leading Marius to barricade. Witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed. Shot broke collar bone. Vigorous hand seized him before consciousness vanished.

**Medical recovery (7 September)**: Doctor declared recovery assured. Marius called grandfather "father" three times; Gillenormand agreed to bring Cosette.

**Cosette's arrival and revelation**: Learned she was not daughter of old man she called father; another Fauchelevent was real father. **Dowry: five hundred eighty thousand francs, constituted legacy by dead person desiring to remain unknown.**

**Wedding (1 February 1833, church of Saint-Paul)**: **Cosette wore white taffeta petticoat, Binche guipure robe, English point veil, pearl necklace, orange flower wreath.** Route: Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire. First coach held Cosette, Aunt Gillenormand, M. Gillenormand, Jean Valjean. Marius came in second coach. **During dinner, Basque reported M. Fauchelevent injured hand paining him; would come tomorrow. Jean Valjean rose, left unperceived during celebration.**

**Jean Valjean's moral crisis post-wedding**: In Cosette's empty bedroom: no sheets, pillow without case. All feminine objects removed. Only Jean Valjean's bed made up. Remained twelve long hours ice-cold, motionless as corpse. Then shuddered convulsively, kissed Cosette's garments.

**Javert's death (evening, Place du Châtelet)**: Took off hat, placed on quay edge. Tall black figure appeared on parapet, bent towards Seine, drew self up, fell straight down. Dull splash followed. Javert drowned. **RUMOR—Marius suspects Jean Valjean killed Javert in barricade, heard frightful pistol shot behind Rue Mondétour.**

**Jean Valjean's revelation and estrangement (17 February morning)**: Very pale, eyes hollow, sunken by sleeplessness. **Proclaimed: "I am an ex-convict."** Justified: conscience implacable; duty places one in hell. Marius shocked, pleaded with him not to tell Cosette. Jean Valjean chose to tell himself.

**Marius's rationalization**: Concluded Jean Valjean horrible workman but admirable work. Dung-heap aids spring to create rose. Adored Cosette, she is light. Jean Valjean is empty chrysalis. Must keep word promised. First duty to Cosette. Acquired knowledge of six hundred thousand francs. Unable to probe out of respect for promised secret. Believed grave duty: restitution to someone sought with discretion. Abstained from touching money.

**Cosette's alienation**: Address as _thou_ replaced by _you_, "Madame," "Monsieur Jean," rendering him another person. She became more gay, less tender. Still loved him sincerely. One day chanced to say "father." Flash of joy illuminated his melancholy countenance. He caught her up: "Say Jean."—She replied: "Ah! truly, Monsieur Jean" with laughter. **"That is right," said he. Turned aside to wipe eyes. This was the last time.** Complete extinction ensued. Marius' estrangement strategy: gradually estranging Jean Valjean from house and effacing him from Cosette's mind. All-powerful magnetism caused Cosette to do instinctively what Marius wished. **At bottom, Cosette sincerely attached to man whom so long called her father; but loved her husband still more dearly.**

**Jean Valjean's withdrawal (late spring/summer 1833)**: Old man neatly clad in black emerged daily at same hour towards nightfall from Rue de l'Homme Armé. Passed Blancs-Manteaux, gained Rue Culture-Sainte-Catherine, reached Rue de l'Écharpe, turned left into Rue Saint-Louis. Soon went only as far as Rue Pavée, shook head, turned back. Then did not overstep Blancs-Manteaux. Head craned forward; chin moved; folds in gaunt neck painful to behold. **He was eighty years old; before Marius' marriage, would have hardly been taken for fifty; that year had counted for thirty.** What he bore on brow was no longer wrinkles of age, but mysterious mark of death. Gazed into space with air of reproach.

**Physical collapse and preparations for death**: Week passed: Jean Valjean had not taken step in room, remained in bed. Made effort to dress in old workingman's clothes, obliged to pause many times. One day descended staircase, took three steps in street, seated himself on post, went upstairs. This was last oscillation of pendulum. Following day did not leave apartment. Day after that, did not leave bed. Took Bishop's candlesticks from chimney-piece, two wax candles from drawer, lighted them though broad daylight, summer time. **[Lamentable cries heard by God alone]: "All is over. I shall never see her more... What is frightful is to die without seeing her."**

**Marius and Cosette's discovery and invitation**: By accident, Marius learned all Jean Valjean had done. Told Jean Valjean: "Your chamber still stands ready in our house." Insisted Jean Valjean part of themselves; he is Cosette's father and Marius's.

**Cosette's plea**: "If you only knew how pretty the garden is now! The azaleas are doing very well there... You shall have your plot in the garden, you shall cultivate it... father, I have had a sorrow, there was a robin redbreast which had made her nest in a hole in the wall, and a horrible cat ate her..."

**Jean Valjean's response and final revelation**: Claims Death is good arrangement; God knows better what we need. **All at once rose to his feet with firm step, detached from wall little copper crucifix suspended there, returned to seat with freedom of movement of perfect health.** Explained Cosette's fortune truly belongs to her. Revealed source: black jet from England, white jet from Norway; invented way of substituting for slides of soldered sheet iron, slides of iron laid together. Six hundred thousand francs made from trade. Also managed very well with glass goods rivalling Berlin jewellery. Adjured Marius: "Have no fear, the six hundred thousand francs really belong to Cosette!"

**Final decline**: Breath became intermittent; little rattling interrupted it. Found difficulty in moving forearm; feet had lost all movement. As wretchedness of limb and feebleness of body increased, all majesty of soul displayed and spread over brow. Light of unknown world already visible in eyes.

## Thénardier's Blackmail Attempt and Marius's Confrontation

**Thénardier's discovery and visit**: Through daughter Azelma tracking married pair, discovered Cosette was Madame la Baronne Pontmercy. Discovered man encountered in Grand Sewer. Wore black cloth coat, silk waistcoat, boots, green glasses, plastered gray hair. **Offered to drive individual from family who has no right there; claimed twenty thousand francs as price.** Marius replied with cold tone, double "I know it."

**Thénardier's exposure and humiliation**: With agility of monkey, tore off spectacles, withdrew two quills from nose, took off face as man takes off hat. **Strangely surprised; bewildered nonetheless.** Baron recognized him thoroughly.

**Marius's knowledge and confrontation**: **Revealed Javert's suicide facts**: Announced two newspapers: _Moniteur_ of 15th June, 1832, announced Javert's suicide, adding Javert reported to prefect that, having been taken prisoner in barricade of Rue de la Chanvrerie, he owed his life to magnanimity of insurgent who, holding him under pistol, fired into air instead of blowing out his brains. **Marius possessed evidence, certain date, irrefragable proof.**

**Marius's speech to Thénardier**: **"You are an infamous wretch! you are a liar, a calumniator, a villain... you have only succeeded in glorifying him. And it is you who are the thief! And it is you who are the assassin! I saw you, Thénardier Jondrette, in that lair on the Rue de l'Hôpital."** Offered twenty thousand francs total, ordered him to America with daughter; wife dead.

**Thénardier's outcome**: **The moral wretchedness of Thénardier was irremediable. He was in America what he had been in Europe. With Marius' money, Thénardier set up as slave-dealer.**

## Père-Lachaise Cemetery

**Jean Valjean's burial**: In cemetery of Père-Lachaise, vicinity of common grave, far from elegant quarter, in deserted corner beside old wall, beneath great yew tree over which climbs wild convolvulus, amid dandelions and mosses, lies stone. Stone no more exempt than others from leprosy of time, dampness, lichens, defilement of birds. Water turns it green, air blackens it. Not near any path; people not fond of walking in that direction because grass high and feet immediately wet. Lizards come thither in little sunshine. All around quivering of weeds. In spring, linnets warble in trees.
